q1: An HTML comment always starts with `<!--` and ends with `-->`; everything between is ignored when the page renders.
q2: `<`, `>`, and `&` are reserved by the HTML parser for tags and entities; `@` has no special meaning in HTML markup.
q3: ` ` renders as a space character that doesn't collapse and doesn't allow a line break at that position — a non-breaking space.
q4: `&` is the named entity for a literal ampersand.
q5: `<`, `>`, `&`, and `©` are real named entities; ` 2;` is not a recognized entity name.
q6: HTML comments can't be nested — the parser closes the comment at the first `-->` it finds, so the text after that point is treated as regular markup.
q7: A valid comment wraps the content between the opening `<!--` and the closing `-->`, in that order.
q8: Comments are visible in page source (not hidden) and cannot be nested; a raw `&` can be misread as starting an entity, regular whitespace collapses to one space, and ` ` blocks a line break — all true.
q9: ` ` does not collapse the way a regular space does, and it also blocks a line break at that position.
q10: Raw `<` and `>` in text content should be escaped as `<` and `>` so the parser doesn't try to interpret them as the start of a tag.
